candidates.abstract: Poxviruses enclose a complete viral transcription machinery alongside their dsDNA genome within the viral core, a transcription-competent compartment delimited by a permeable multi-layered protein shell. Upon infection of a cell and core release, this machinery almost immediately starts synthesizing early mRNAs, which are extruded across the core wall into the cytoplasm for translation. While in vitro structures of the isolated viral DNA-dependent RNA polymerase (vRNAP) have been described1–3, its native in virio architecture, spatial organization, and physical coupling to the genome remain unknown. Using cryo-electron tomography and sub-tomogram averaging on purified Vaccinia virus cores, we reveal that packaged vRNAP exists not as monomer, but as massive 1.8 MDa resting-state dimer bridged by fully ordered vaccinia virus early transcription factor (VETF). We also identify a subpopulation of these dimers bound to the essential kinase VPK2 and the core protein L4, which directly tether the transcribing engines to the packaged genome near the inner core wall. Furthermore, we determine a sub-nanometer structure of the putative poxvirus mRNA extrusion portal complex, revealing a rigid assembly integrated into the core wall comprising an E8 hexameric crown, an E6 hexameric central hub, and a basal L3 dodecameric channel suited for nucleic acid export. Together, these structures provide a comprehensive architectural blueprint of important components of the poxvirus core and open new structural and functional avenues for investigating poxvirus genome packaging, transcription activation, and mRNA extrusion.

candidates.title: Continuous N-to-C Peptide Synthesis
candidates.authors: Jingjun Yin, Ji Qi, Zhiyan Song, Baoqiang Wan, Jin Zhang, Fangzhou Xie, Enkai Wang, Yang Cao, Hongming Li, Qixue Yuan, Jinxiang He, Xiao Wang, Liwen Xu, Chunrui Sun, Kai-Jiong Xiao, Feng Peng, Shishi Lin, Gao Shang, Lu Wang, Jing Xu, Jiwen Jiang, Xiupeng Duan, Donghong Li, Mengli Zhang, Haijiang Nan, Like Chen, Fang Wang, Tong Kang, Minyi Feng, Guiquan Liu, Louis-Charles Campeau
candidates.abstract: Current state-of-the-art peptide synthesis faces a significant global challenge in efficiency and sustainability.1 With demand for peptide therapeutics growing rapidly,2,3 our ability to provide these important medicines is under increasing pressure.4 Chemical synthesis typically proceeds C-to-N and requires protecting groups, whereas ribosomal synthesis proceeds N-to-C from unprotected amino acids (AAs). To improve efficiency and sustainability, we developed a continuous N-to-C Peptide Synthesis (NCPS) using N-/C-unprotected AAs or fragments without intermediate isolations, achieving ≥95% average yield per coupling and ≤1.0% epimerization. The method enabled seven consecutive couplings. Starting from N-/C-unprotected AAs, peptide assembly requires fewer isolations than those needed to prepare the corresponding Fmoc-AA building blocks before conventional synthesis can begin. This method accepts all 20 canonical AAs and a wide range of non-canonical AAs important for drug-like profiles.5 Longer peptides can be readily assembled through continuous fragment coupling while maintaining chiral integrity. This approach reduces isolations by ~10-fold and waste generation by up to ~100-fold. We further developed a flow synthesizer that enhances speed and productivity while mitigating batch manufacturing risks. The method enabled the synthesis of a tirzepatide heptapeptide fragment, degarelix, a 14-mer engineered macrocyclic peptide, and semaglutide. Overall, continuous NCPS has the potential to transform peptide manufacturing.

candidates.title: Hexa-substituted benzene synthesis with non-classical carbocations
candidates.authors: Guillaume Mollaert, Hang-Fei Tu, Jacob R. King, Mihai V. Popescu, Zexian Li, Quan Zhang, Eric Palomo, Robert S. Paton, Marcos G. Suero
candidates.abstract: Benzene rings are the most frequently encountered ring system in small-molecule drugs1. However, benzenes with six substituents are notably absent from small molecule libraries, owing to challenges associated with their synthesis and the limited availability of commercially available aromatic building blocks2. Therefore, new chemical processes that enable their synthesis with predictable regiochemical control and broad substituent diversity could enable medicinal chemists to explore this uncharted aromatic chemical space in hit-to-lead and lead optimization campaigns. Herein, we describe a highly modular and programmable platform for accessing hexa-substituted benzene rings from aromatic cyclopropenium cations and (trialkylsilyl)allenes, with precise control over all six benzene positions encoded in the starting materials. The exceptional regioselectivity observed originates from the selective evolution of an unusual non-classical carbocation featuring four-centre four-electron bonding as revealed by density functional theory calculations. Our benzannulation enables the selective installation of synthetic handles that were exploited for the synthesis of previously inaccessible penta- and hexa-substituted analogues of the anticancer drug sonidegib and the antihypertensive drug telmisartan, as well as the polyaromatic hydrocarbon triphenylene. Notably, the use of enantiopure allenes unlocks a new route to enantioenriched multi-substituted biaryls through our benzannulation occurring with “memory of chirality”.

candidates.title: Quasi-degenerate cation occupation enables oxygen-vacancy defect healing in nonlinear optical crystals
candidates.authors: Jinfeng Han, Fei Liang, Kui Wu, Dazhi Lu, Deliang Cui, Haohai Yu, Huaijin Zhang
candidates.abstract: Abstract Chemical substitution is an effective strategy to enhance the desired performances of materials based on known structural prototypes. However, it almost invariably introduces intrinsic defects, such as vacancies and twinning defects, which couple with dopants and obscure or degrade the intrinsic properties. Therefore, chemical substitution that enables atomically precise engineering of materials without generating defect structures remains challenging. Here, we propose a quasi-degenerate cation occupation strategy to overcome this detrimental coupling and successfully apply it to the langasite-family nonlinear optical (NLO) crystal, La 3 TiGa 5 O 14 (LGTi). Therein, the cross-site occupation of Ti and Ti 3+ /Ti 4+ redox flexibility improves the kinetic accessibility of oxygen-vacancy ( V O ) defects associated with cation disorder, enabling their removal during oxidative annealing. The oxidized LGTi single crystal has a V O -related defect concentration below the electron paramagnetic resonance detection limit, with a laser damage threshold of 2.53 GW/cm 2 and a large NLO coefficient of 3.51 pm/V, both exceeding the previously reported values for bulk langasite-family crystals. Overall, this work provides a quasi-degenerate cation occupation strategy to mitigate substitution-induced defects in structurally complex crystalline systems and has great prospects in enhancing material performance.

candidates.title: ORE1 stabilizes PIF4 protein through a UBP12/UBP13-dependent regulatory module in thermomorphogenesis
candidates.authors: Su-Hyun Park, Teck Lim Moo, Nam-Hai Chua
candidates.abstract: Understanding how plants integrate developmental programs with temperature-responsive growth remains a central challenge in plant biology. Here, we uncover a mechanism by which a canonical leaf senescence regulator directly governs thermomorphogenesis in Arabidopsis. We show that ORESARA1 (ORE1), best known for orchestrating leaf senescence, promotes warm temperature-induced hypocotyl and petiole elongation and the expression of warmth-responsive genes IAA19 and YUC8. Mechanistically, ORE1 acts upstream of PHYTOCHROME INTERACTING FACTOR 4 (PIF4), the central transcriptional hub for thermomorphogenesis. ORE1 does not alter PIF4 transcript abundance but specifically stabilizes PIF4 protein under warmth by physically interacting with PIF4 in the nucleus to enhance its deubiquitination. We identify the deubiquitinase UBP12/UBP13 as an essential component of this pathway; however, PIF4 does not bind UBP12/UBP13 directly. Biochemical and genetic analyses demonstrate that ORE1 functions as a molecular scaffold, recruiting PIF4 to an ORE1-UBP12/UBP13 complex to position UBP12/UBP13 for PIF4 deubiquitination. This UBP12/UBP13-ORE1-PIF4 module establishes a paradigm where a senescence factor regulates thermomorphogenesis by orchestrating deubiquitinase-mediated tuning of PIF4 proteostasis. Plants adapt their growth to warmth, but how aging signals tune protein stability remains unclear. Here, the authors show that the senescence factor ORE1 acts as a scaffold to stabilize the heat regulator PIF4 via UBP12/UBP13-mediated deubiquitination, driving warmth induced growth.

candidates.title: ALKR1275Q expands Schwann cell precursor-like cells during sympathoadrenal commitment, creating a permissive state for neuroblastoma initiation
candidates.authors: Mingzhi Liu, Panagiotis Alkinoos Polychronopoulos, Yiming Xia, Ann-Sophie Oppelt, Ana Marin Navarro, Tzu-Po Chuang, Veronica Zubillaga, Huaitao Cheng, Qirong Lin, Lola Boutin, Mercè Baulenas-Farrés, Jinhye Ryu, Leilei Zhou, Hugo Metzger, Martin Enge, Daniel Bexell, John Inge Johnsen, Oscar C. candidates.abstract: Abstract Neuroblastoma (NB) arises from neural crest-derived cells of the sympathoadrenal lineage, yet how predisposing genetic lesions influence early human development remains poorly understood. Here, we use patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) models carrying the familial ALK R1275Q mutation to investigate its role during sympathoadrenal differentiation. We show that ALK R1275Q delays lineage maturation and sustains a proliferative progenitor state characterized by elevated ALK signaling and expansion of a Schwann cell precursor (SCP)-like population. This SCP-like state persists during differentiation and is reduced by ALK inhibition or CRISPR-based mutation correction. Although ALK R1275Q alone is insufficient to drive tumor formation in vivo, it enhances susceptibility to oncogenic transformation in cooperation with MYCN. Together, these findings support a model in which ALK R1275Q reshapes developmental trajectories by maintaining a proliferative SCP-like progenitor state, thereby creating a permissive cellular context for NB initiation.

candidates.title: Longitudinal changes in mis-splicing in a cohort of female twins are widespread and highlight mechanisms of ageing
candidates.authors: Dongmeng Wang, Yasrab N. Raza, Amy L. Roberts, Ruth C. E. Bowyer, Anna Ramisch, Max Tomlinson, Christopher J. Shore, Xinyu Yan, Emmanouil T. Dermitzakis, Claire J. Steves, Jordana T. Bell, Cristina Menni, Julia S. El-Sayed Moustafa, Kerrin S. Small
candidates.abstract: Abstract Ageing is characterised by widespread cellular and molecular dysregulation including broad changes to gene expression. To study the impact of ageing on alternative splicing we profiled whole-blood RNA-seq data from 318 female twins (median age 61) at three time points over 6-8 years. We observe longitudinal changes across multiple classes of alternative splicing. Notably, intron retention, a marker of mis-splicing, shows a striking increase over time ( P = 5.2 × 10 −5 ). Twin modelling demonstrates that intron retention within an individual is heritable, with heritability increasing from 0.44 to 0.55 over time. Intron retention levels inversely associate with expression of RNA-binding proteins including SRSF4 , ELAVL1 , and AGO1 , and show time-varying positive associations with diabetes status and markers of kidney disease, suggesting a link to chronic disease. Together, these findings suggest that mis-splicing is a heritable feature of human ageing which increases in prevalence over time and is associated with age-related disease.

candidates.title: Non Hermitian synthetic phase shifter with topologically protected phase control via tunable losses
candidates.authors: Kevin Zelaya, Jonathan Friedman, Hector A. Rubio Rivera, Stefan Preble, Mohammad-Ali Miri
candidates.abstract: Phase shifters are fundamental reconfigurable components in photonic circuits. In conjunction with passive elements, they control light flow and serve as foundational building blocks for diverse applications, including communication, sensing, analog signal processing, and quantum control. Conventional phase shifters achieve phase control by modulating the refractive index through various physical mechanisms such as thermo-optic or electro-optic effects. However, despite expectations that such index–based approaches would integrate seamlessly, they, in practice, restrict circuit size, bandwidth, and scalability and thus become bottlenecks to large–scale photonic integration. Here, we introduce an alternative phase–control approach based on optical loss modulation. We demonstrate a synthetic phase shifter that uses two independently controlled loss–modulation stages combined with multipath interference to achieve full–cycle phase tunability while maintaining constant amplitude. We develop a theoretical framework based on conserved topological charges to show how synthetic phase control can be achieved via non-Hermitian effects, enabling robust, topologically protected phase control. By shifting the paradigm from index control to loss modulation, the proposed synthetic phase shifter could pave the way for scalable integrated photonic systems that support applications from communications and sensing to photonic classical and quantum information processing. Programmable photonic circuits typically rely on refractive-index modulation for active control, limiting scalability. Here, authors develop and validate a synthetic phase-shifter framework using optical loss modulation to achieve full-cycle phase control protected by topological quantities.

candidates.authors: Justina McEvoy, Melody Allensworth-James, Mariajose Franco, Shannon Sweeney, Natalie Geiger, Juliette Kippen, Asha Jacob Jannu, Stefan Atkinson, Ayush Attery, Nathaniel Twarog, Chen He, Shay Sneed, Åsa Karlström, Cynthia Cline, Cody Ramirez, Antonia Chroni, Hongjian Jin, Yiping Fan, Gang Wu, Beisi Xu, Abbas Shirinifard, Jackie Norrie, Brittney Gordon, Kaitlin Lord, JaKayla Johnson, Madison Parks, Heather Sheppard, George Campbell, Jennifer L. Dyer
candidates.abstract: Abstract Most pediatric solid tumor cell lines were established decades ago, and patient-matched organoids and xenografts are rarely available, limiting their translational utility. We present an approach to generate triads of patient-matched xenografts, three-dimensional organoids, and two-dimensional primary cultures from pediatric tumors, including rhabdomyosarcoma, osteosarcoma, neuroblastoma, Ewing sarcoma, Wilms tumor, and retinoblastoma. We have generated organoids from 135 pediatric tumors, alongside 82 patient-matched two-dimensional primary cultures and 20 new cell lines. When orthotopically implanted into immunocompromised mice, these models preserved the molecular and cellular features of the original patient tumor. We completed 365 single-cell and single-nucleus RNA-sequencing experiments encompassing over 2.2 million cells to evaluate cellular heterogeneity across triads. All samples are renewable, and over 3000 vials have been cryopreserved for unrestricted distribution through the Childhood Solid Tumor Network. In this work, we present a comprehensive methodological toolbox for generating patient-matched triads for advancing preclinical pediatric cancer research.

candidates.title: Spatiotemporal brain dynamics of limb ownership perception
candidates.authors: Maximilian F. A. Hauser, Sara Coppi, Daniel Lundqvist, H. Henrik Ehrsson
candidates.abstract: Abstract We experience our limbs as our own, but how does the brain generate this fundamental sense of body ownership? Previous studies have relied mainly on fMRI or lesion mapping, providing a static view of the neural mechanisms underlying body ownership. Using magnetoencephalography, robotically controlled visuotactile stimulation, and multivariate analysis across the rubber hand illusion, a real hand condition, and multiple control conditions, we identified source vector dissimilarity patterns reflecting ownership of the left arm. Three phases of ownership-specific activity patterns emerged: (i) anticipatory patterns in medial frontal cortex, right posterior parietal cortex, and right posterior cerebellum before tactile stimulation; (ii) multisensory integration patterns in right dorsal and ventral premotor cortex, right posterior parietal cortex, and anterior cerebellum at 116–156 ms poststimulus; and (iii) later bilateral insular and left hemisphere patterns at 184–232 ms. These findings provide a whole-brain, time-resolved map of activity patterns underlying body ownership, revealing its dynamic neural construction.

candidates.title: Marine volatile organic compounds air-sea exchange dynamics across a summer-to-autumn ecosystem transition
candidates.authors: Mehrshad Foroughan, Thomas Holst, Kaisa Kraft, Martti Honkanen, Lauri Laakso, Heidi Hellén, Jukka Seppälä, Ken Stenbäck, Christa Marandino, Riikka Rinnan
candidates.abstract: Marine ecosystems influence atmospheric chemistry and climate by exchanging volatile organic compounds (VOCs) with the atmosphere, yet the chemical diversity and the environmental controls of the exchanged compounds remain poorly constrained. This gap persists because most marine observations are targeted, short-term, and narrow-suite measurements that seldom deliver chemically broad, continuous fluxes. Here we show that marine VOC exchange is chemically diverse and changes in magnitude and composition on event‑to‑season timescales. Using continuous flux measurements of 73 m/z features in the Baltic Sea, we observe a pronounced reorganization of net exchange: early organosulfur emissions diminish as cyanobacterial biomass declines (indicating water-side source limitation), while oxygenated and nitrogen-containing VOCs exhibit mixed behaviors ranging from deposition to episodic emissions (often dominated by wind-driven gas transfer kinetics). Together, these results demonstrate that chemically diverse marine VOC exchange is closely coupled to wind-induced mixing, water‑column structure, and phytoplankton community succession, highlighting the need to resolve these dynamic ecosystem states to predict future atmospheric composition. Continuous measurements of air-sea exchange at a Baltic Sea island reveal how phytoplankton and physical processes together shape the release and uptake of diverse volatile organic compounds as summer turns to autumn.

candidates.title: CARM1-mediated methylation controls interactions of ALIX with key partners important for cytokinesis
candidates.authors: Solène Huard, Samyuktha Suresh, Anđela Petrović, Virginie Maire, Léa Surcouf, Rayan Dakroub, Christine Chatellard, Jessica Vayr, Sonia Ruggiero, Yara Hajj Younes, Vanessa Masson, Patrick Poullet, Michael Richard, Kardelen Gökçen, Clémence Vissotsky, Louise Amara, Rayane Dibsy, Julie Thomsen, Lucid Belmudes, Ahmed El Marjou, Rémy Sadoul, Winfried Weissenhorn, Yohann Couté, Damarys Loew, Raphaël Guérois, Nicolas Reynoird, Arnaud Echard, Thierry Dubois
candidates.abstract: CARM1 is an arginine methyltransferase with a well-established role in regulating gene expression, but its cytoplasmic functions remain largely uncharacterized. Here, we identified ALIX, a cytoplasmic protein acting with the ESCRT-III machinery in numerous membrane remodeling events, as a partner and substrate of CARM1. We demonstrate that CARM1 methylates arginine residues within the proline-rich motif of ALIX. At the molecular level, ALIX methylation impairs SH3-dependent association with CD2AP, CIN85, and endophilin-A2 that are required for cytokinesis. Using a mutant of ALIX that is unable to bind these proteins, we further show that these interactions are essential for ALIX functions during cytokinesis. Mechanistically, ALIX methylation controls the levels of CD2AP at the cytokinetic midbody, which are known to be critical for successful cytokinesis. Altogether, this work highlights the significance of arginine methylation as a regulatory post-translational modification important for the final step of cell division, by modulating interactions between proline-rich domains and their SH3-containing partners. ALIX methylation by CARM1 controls CD2AP levels at the midbody and is important for cytokinesis. Their findings reveal a role for protein arginine methylation in the last step of cell division.

candidates.title: 3D-printed Eutectic high-entropy alloys with dynamic protection for tribological damage resistance
candidates.authors: Dongpeng Hua, Lin Zhou, Ying Li, Jianbao Zhang, Weibing Wang, Xuhui Pei, Longhui Zhu, Xiangren Bai, Jingchen Wang, Sida Liu, Qing Zhou, Haifeng Wang, Jian Lu
candidates.abstract: Maintaining the structural integrity of metallic materials under extreme localized shear poses a significant challenge for engineering reliability in the aerospace, automotive, and energy sectors, as such loading readily triggers catastrophic strain localization and surface delamination. Here, we report a nanoarchitecture-driven dynamic protection strategy to overcome this challenge. We engineer an FCC-dominant nanolamellar (FCC-NL) architecture in an AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy (EHEA) by combining additive manufacturing (AM) with metastability engineering. Rather than undergoing the structural degradation observed in conventional EHEAs, this AM-enabled FCC-NL architecture orchestrates a robust hierarchical protective structure under severe sliding. It concurrently drives the bottom-up mechanochemical assembly of a damage-tolerant amorphous-nanocrystalline γ-Fe2O3 tribolayer and the top-down mechanical assembly of a strain-isolating nacre-like subsurface. This synergy yields a wear rate of 5.8 × 10−6 mm3 N−1 m−1, achieving an order-of-magnitude enhancement in surface damage resistance that surpasses currently reported values for bulk HEAs. This dynamic protection concept provides a design framework for developing highly surface-damage-tolerant alloys, essential to the reliability of critical engineering systems. Alloys with high tribological damage resistance are critical for advanced engineering. The authors propose a nanoarchitecture-driven dynamic protection concept to achieve this, demonstrating the concept in 3D-printed eutectic high-entropy alloys.

candidates.abstract: Hybrid glasses of coordination polymers promise a fusion of processability and structural functionality, yet their formation is limited by poor thermal stability and high melting points. Here, the authors report mesophase-induced vitrification in magnesium-based frameworks, enabling glass formation without melting while preserving network integrity and mechanical stiffness.

candidates.title: Eco-evolutionary dynamics of active virus-host interactions in a freshwater lake revealed through metaHi-C
candidates.authors: Francisco Nadal-Molero, Ana-Belen Martin-Cuadrado, Maliheh Mehrshad
candidates.abstract: Abstract Detecting active phage–bacteria interactions in natural microbial communities remains a major limitation for understanding their ecological dynamics and associated co-evolutionary processes. Here, we apply metaHi-C, a chromosome conformation capture method, to resolve active virus–host associations in a freshwater microbial community. From >900 microbial and >33,000 viral Hi-C–assembled genomes, we identify 100 high-confidence phage–host linkages spanning major freshwater bacterial lineages, including Limnohabitans , Acidimicrobium , Synechococcus , Candidatus Nanopelagicus, Candidatus Planktophila, Candidatus Methylopumilus, and Polynucleobacter . The inferred networks reveal signatures consistent with diverse infection patterns, including broad-host-range phages, cellular-level co-infection, kill-the-winner-like dynamics, and one-to-one interactions. These ecological patterns are associated with signatures of diversifying selection in host-interaction genes, consistent with host-range expansion, alongside conserved genomic regions in broad-host-range and co-infecting phages, indicating functional constraints on essential infection modules. Together, these results demonstrate that metaHi-C enables the direct detection of active phage–host associations within a community snapshot, and that, when combined with longitudinal metagenomic recruitment analyses, this approach can link community-level infection dynamics to underlying evolutionary processes, revealing how these forces shape population dynamics of freshwater bacteria.

candidates.abstract: Abstract Color center spins in diamond nanostructures are a key resource for emerging quantum technologies. Their innate surface proximity makes precise control of diamond surface chemistry essential for optimizing their functionality and charge states. However, conventional surface functionalization methods provide limited control over the resulting surface termination and color-center charge state. Here, we demonstrate nonvolatile tuning of diamond’s surface termination through laser-induced oxidation of H-terminated diamond nanopillars. By tracking negatively charged silicon-vacancy (SiV − ) photoluminescence as a charge-state proxy, we elucidate the carrier-assisted nature of this photocatalytic process through systematic photon-flux and photon-energy analyses, identifying defect charge cycling as a source of photogenerated carriers that drive the interfacial redox chemistry responsible for surface oxidation. Our results suggest that this approach may be applicable to other color centers and host materials for charge-state control and surface engineering in solid-state quantum devices.

candidates.authors: Haobin Song, Yang-Feng Cui, Nan Zhao, Yue Wang, Yifan Li, Wenjing Li, Cong Huang, Hui Ying Yang
candidates.abstract: Vanadium-based positive electrodes for aqueous batteries offer high-capacity, low-cost energy storage but are limited by vanadium dissolution and sluggish kinetics. Amorphization alleviates kinetic limitations by creating open ion-transport pathways, yet vanadium dissolution remains unresolved. Here, we propose a coordination-engineering strategy that stabilizes amorphous vanadium oxides via fluorine incorporation, thereby suppressing vanadium dissolution without compromising fast ion-transport kinetics. Replacing O2- with highly electronegative F- converts labile σ + π V-O coordination into robust σ-dominated V-F coordination. Consequently, aqueous zinc-ion batteries assembled with the fluorinated amorphous vanadium oxide positive electrode exhibit fast kinetics and long-term cycling stability, delivering a high specific capacity of 155.6 mAh g−1 at 200 A g−1, stable cycling for up to 70,000 cycles at 100 A g−1, and durable operation at 0.1 A g−1 (20 mg cm−2) for over six months. This work shows that fluorine-induced reconstruction of the local coordination environment can resolve the stability-kinetics trade-off in amorphous electrodes, providing a microscopic-to-macroscopic design principle for aqueous batteries. Amorphous vanadium oxides can store zinc rapidly but often suffer from structural instability in water. Here, authors use fluorine coordination to stabilize the local vanadium environment while preserving fast ion transport, enabling durable aqueous zinc batteries.

candidates.title: LitMOF: An LLM Multi-Agent for Literature-Validated Metal-Organic Frameworks Database Correction and Expansion
candidates.authors: Honghui Kim, Dohoon Kim, Jihan Kim
candidates.abstract: Metal–organic framework databases have grown rapidly through experimental deposition and large-scale literature extraction, yet recent analyses indicate that nearly half of their entries contain substantial structural errors. These errors propagate through high-throughput screening and machine-learning workflows, limiting the reliability of data-driven materials discovery. Repairing them is difficult because the necessary evidence is scattered across crystallographic files, synthesis descriptions, and the primary literature. Here we present LitMOF, a multi-agent framework driven by large language models that reads the original publication for each structure and cross-validates it against the deposited entry to repair errors. Applying LitMOF to the metal–organic framework subset of the Cambridge Structural Database, we assembled LitMOF-DB, a curated set of 189,567 computation-ready structures that includes 9,277 repaired entries, or 69.1% of the not-computation-ready structures in the latest CoRE MOF database. The system also recovered 8,771 synthesized but undeposited frameworks missing from existing resources. Using direct air capture screening as a case study, we show that structural errors distort predicted adsorption energies and CO2/H2O selectivity, which misranks materials, produces false positives, and omits high-performing candidates. candidates.title: Diffusive Dynamics of Nonstabilizerness
candidates.authors: Zhenyu Xiao, Shinsei Ryu
candidates.abstract: Symmetries shape the quantum-information dynamics of many-body systems, but their effect on nonstabilizerness, the resource complementary to entanglement, is less understood. We compute the stabilizer Renyi entropy, a measure of nonstabilizerness, in U(1)-symmetric one-dimensional random circuits. The disorder-averaged dynamics is captured by a four-replica tensor network, which we evaluate by S4-adapted infinite time-evolving block decimation (iTEBD) directly in the thermodynamic limit. Together with a hydrodynamic argument, our results identify a diffusive universality class for the late-time approach of nonstabilizerness to its random-state value, with the stabilizer Renyi entropy gap closing as 1/t. The same scaling is verified in an energy-conserving nonintegrable Ising chain. More broadly, our framework provides a hydrodynamic perspective on nonstabilizerness generation and offers insight into the design of approximate Haar-random states in Hamiltonian dynamics.

candidates.title: Syndrome Resampling Enhances Quantum Error Correction Thresholds
candidates.authors: Luis Colmenarez, Áron Márton, Markus Müller
candidates.abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) enables fault-tolerant quantum computation but requires operating quantum hardware at physical error rates below code-dependent thresholds, which remains challenging for current devices. We introduce , a general method that increases QEC thresholds of any decoder and suppresses logical errors without additional hardware, decoding modifications, or code-specific assumptions beyond syndrome statistics. The method exploits the fact that syndromes with low probability are likely to lead to logical failure; therefore, biasing syndrome averages toward most likely syndromes effectively increases logical fidelities. We establish a direct connection between the Rényi coherent information (RCI) and powers of the syndrome probability distribution, showing that resampling syndromes according to these powers combined with maximum likelihood decoding (MLD) realizes a family of optimal thresholds associated with phase transitions in the RCI. Numerical simulations of surface codes demonstrate that syndrome resampling substantially increases thresholds for both optimal and suboptimal decoders and reduces logical error rates by up to four orders of magnitude in experimentally relevant regimes. We further show that syndrome resampling can be effectively implemented from finite data and combined with decoding-based postselection to achieve additional gains. Finally, applying the method to existing experimental QEC data yields up to 2 orders of magnitude reduction in logical error rates without requiring additional measurements. Our results provide a practical and decoder-agnostic route to improved logical fidelities in near-term QEC experiments.

candidates.authors: Kotaro Tanaka, Daemo Kang, Naotaka Yoshikawa, Fumiya Sekiguchi, Hirotaka Terai, Takahiro Morimoto, Ryo Shimano
candidates.abstract: Understanding how angular momentum is exchanged between different degrees of freedom has long been a subject of fundamental interest, as represented by the Einstein-de Haas effect in a ferromagnet, in which a change of rotational speed of the rigid body is induced by a change of magnetization. Here, we report the imprinting of orbital angular momentum (OAM) of light to a superconductor, a macroscopic quantum state of fermionic condensate, through the Higgs mode excitation by a terahertz (THz) vortex beam. By using spatiotemporally resolved THz-pump and THz-probe spectroscopy, we observe a rotating order parameter oscillation in which the phase structure of the vortex beam is imprinted onto the Higgs mode. Time-dependent Ginzburg–Landau analysis shows that the rotating Higgs mode carries a finite OAM. This work opens a pathway for imprinting OAM of light onto a superconductor and manipulating its order parameter.

candidates.title: Giant Room-Temperature Magnetoelectric Coupling Effect in Nanocomposite Thin Films via Strain-Sensitive Polarization
candidates.authors: Hao Li, Yali Yang, Shiqing Deng, Yajun Qi, Peng Wang, He Qi, Huifen Yu, Yuan Zhang, Yu Chen, Jiaou Wang, Jianghua Chen, Jiangyu Li, Junling Wang, Jun Chen
candidates.abstract: Magnetoelectric multiferroic composites, which combine ferroelectric and ferromagnetic phases, are pivotal for next-generation electronic devices. Conventional design strategies prioritize ferroelectric materials with large spontaneous polarization to achieve strong magnetoelectric coupling. Here, we propose a paradigm-shifting approach that instead utilizes a material’s high strain sensitivity of polarization. The quantum paraelectric SrTiO3 is discovered as an ideal ferroelectric component due to its exceptionally high polarization response to strain, far exceeding that of classical ferroelectrics like BaTiO3 or PbTiO3. To demonstrate this concept, the desired SrTiO3-NiO nanocomposite films featuring ordered nanopillar array and atomically sharp vertical interfaces were fabricated. This nanostructure maximizes the interfacial contact area and ensures highly efficient strain transfer. The resulting composite exhibits a giant direct magnetoelectric coupling coefficient of 3200 mV/(cm·Oe) at room temperature, demonstrating a remarkably strong macroscopic magnetoelectric response compared with conventional 1-3 composite oxide multiferroic systems. Through a combination of atomic-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy and first-principles calculations, we reveal the outstanding performance originates from the unique strain-sensitive polarization of SrTiO3, which can effectively trigger substantial polarization variations via magnetic field-induced strain transfer across coherent interface. This work redefines the design principle for high-performance magnetoelectric composites by emphasizing strain sensitivity over large polarization, opening a new pathway for developing ultra-sensitive sensors and multi-state, low-power memory devices.

candidates.title: Einstein’s Equation as a Geometric Encoding of Correlations with Quantum Reference Frames
candidates.authors: Eduardo O. Dias
candidates.abstract: In general relativity, the metric field describes spacetime intervals between events relative to any ideal material reference frame as if the frame were not present; in this sense, the metric encodes these intervals. In quantum mechanics, by contrast, such events are naturally accompanied by correlations with that frame. Motivated by this complementarity, we propose a geometry-information equivalence hypothesis (GIEH), according to which the metric field geometrically encodes the relational information otherwise carried by correlations with a local reference frame (LRF). In a small geodesic ball, the GIEH yields the full nonlinear Einstein equation when ideal-LRF conditions are imposed, without assuming an AdS background or an underlying CFT. The framework further allows background correlations to provide an informational origin for the cosmological constant, with their local mutual-information density equal to the Gibbons-Hawking entropy per unit thermodynamic volume.

candidates.authors: Ekaterina Vlasiuk, Manfred Salmhofer, Eugene Demler, Richard Schmidt
candidates.abstract: We investigate how the strong coupling of a superconductor to thermal bosons can enhance its superconducting critical temperature. To tackle this problem, we use a renormalization group approach that allows us to describe the density fluctuations-induced attraction between fermions, capturing the mutual influence of bosonic and fermionic sectors. The self-consistent renormalization group framework predicts a robust increase of the critical temperature across a wide range of interactions. However, this enhancement is progressively suppressed as the system approaches the unitary limit, and therefore the intrinsic upper bound on the critical temperature of the unitary Fermi gas cannot be overcome. We find a nontrivial dependence of the critical temperature on the boson mass and we establish a phase diagram for enhanced superconductivity driven by bosons being either in the condensed or thermal state. We outline possible experimental realizations in cold atomic systems and discuss implementations using electron-exciton mixtures in van der Waals material heterostructures.

candidates.authors: Egor Kovlakov, Rene Gerritsma
candidates.abstract: We perform laser spectroscopy of a trapped ion that is not directly laser cooled. An ultracold atomic bath continuously cools the internal degrees of freedom of the ion to its hyperfine ground state via spin-exchange collisions while a co-trapped 174 Yb + ion sympathetically cools the external degrees of freedom. Successful laser excitation is detected via state-selective charge transfer following a collision with an atom and subsequent ion loss. As a demonstration of this spectroscopic technique, we probe the 6 2 S 1 / 2 → 6 2 P 3 / 2 transition at 329~nm in 173 Yb + and measure the magnetic and electric hyperfine interaction constants for the 6 2 P 3 / 2 state to be A = − 241 ( 1 ) ~MHz and B = 1460 ( 8 ) ~MHz, respectively. Our results are in agreement with a previous measurement obtained in a hollow-cathode discharge experiment but are a factor of 6–9 more precise. The techniques demonstrated in this work may be extended to perform precision spectroscopy on ions with complex level structures with applications in fundamental physics.

This configuration effectively forms a three-level system comprising the electronic ground state and the nuclear ground (g) and isomeric (m) states, resulting in strongly enhanced nuclear hyperfine mixing. Within this framework, a unified analysis of precision measurements on both ions enables the simultaneous determination of five key nuclear parameters without relying on external nuclear inputs: the magnetic dipole moments µg and µm, the bare-nucleus transition energy ωn, the charge-radius difference δ⟨r[2]⟩gm, and the M1 transition matrix element TM1. With this approach, the uncertainties in ωn and δ⟨r[2]⟩gm are estimated to be reduced by factors of 3 and 2, respectively, relative to their current uncertainties. This work could provide a useful benchmark for nuclear theory and serve as a foundation for future development of a [229]Th-based nuclear optical clock.

candidates.authors: Tien Vo, Robert Ergun, Alexandros Chasapis, Oreste Pezzi, Andrea Larosa, Sergio Servidio, Luca Sorriso-Valvo, Le Viet Anh Doan, Paul Cassak, Trevor Bowen, Yi Qi
candidates.abstract: In collisionless plasmas, the particle distributions are often far from local thermodynamic equilibrium, providing a significant source of free energy that leads to complex velocity-space dynamics. In turbulent plasmas, the possibility of a cascade of the free energy in velocity space, analogous to the spatial cascade of fluid and electromagnetic field energies, has been suggested. However, observational evidence of plasma turbulence throughout phase space remains limited. Using measurements from the mission in a special campaign in Earth’s magnetosheath, we present the first statistical study of signatures consistent with velocity-space turbulence across a wide range of plasma conditions. We observe two main populations in the ion velocity-space spectrum: an isotropic − 3 / 2 spectrum and an anisotropic − 2 spectrum organized by the ion β and bulk flow. In addition, the spectral power laws in the spatial and velocity domains are uncorrelated, while the velocity-space spectral index is correlated with estimated real-space energy transfer rates. These results reveal how the ion spectral properties are systematically organized by plasma conditions and related to real-space turbulence. This connection has broad implications for turbulence and the energy partition between thermal and nonthermal particles in space and astrophysical plasmas.

candidates.title: Allee Effect in Compressible Flows
candidates.authors: Jonathan Bauermann, Roberto Benzi, David R. Nelson, Federico Toschi
candidates.abstract: Microbes in marine environments are often confined to thin near-surface layers while being advected by turbulent flows. Because such constrained advection generates an effectively compressible flow, reproduction and transport interact in a nontrivial way. Here, we focus on populations whose growth is governed by an Allee effect and show that sinks and sources, generated by the compressible flow, have dramatic consequences for the survival of such species. We derive analytical expressions for the carrying capacity as a function of the Allee strength in the limit of small and large Damköhler number, which measures the product of the large eddy turnover time and the organism growth rate. Numerical simulations reveal how these two limits connect. In the limit of small Damköhler number, we find a maximal Allee strength, set by the statistics of the compressible flow, that leads to species extinction in fully developed turbulence.

The reasons for this deviation, like the value of the nucleon effective mass m * m and the density dependence of G ′ 0 , are investigated. candidates.title: Systematic Magnetic Structure Generation Based on Oriented Spin Space Groups: Formulation, Applications, and High-Throughput First-Principles Calculations
candidates.authors: Takuya Nomoto, Kohei Shinohara, Hikaru Watanabe, Ryotaro Arita
candidates.abstract: We propose a framework for generating magnetic structures, inspired by the concept of oriented spin space groups (SSGs): Magnetic structures are first generated as totally symmetric representations of an SSG and are then rotated such that they belong to the maximal magnetic space group of the SSG, which we term spin-symmetry-adapted (SSA) structures and oriented SSA structures, respectively. This is a natural framework to enforce fixed magnetic moment magnitudes on the symmetry-equivalent sites as well as to exploit the spin-orbit coupling (SOC)-induced hierarchy of energy scales. To examine the present scheme, we analyze the MAGNDATA database and find that 77% of the reported structures are reproducible at the SSG level, among which 82% are fully reproduced within the oriented SSG scheme, regardless of their spin-only group types or propagation vectors. When the k index is fixed to its experimental value, the number of magnetic structures generated is on average about nine, also demonstrating the high efficiency of this scheme. Next, to quantitatively assess computational and predictive performance, we perform spin density functional theory calculations for 283 materials, first carrying out self-consistent calculations for SSA structures without SOC, followed by fixed-charge calculations including SOC for the descendant oriented SSA structures. The experimental magnetic structures are reproduced as energetically most stable in 83% of cases at the SSG level without SOC and in 76% of cases at the oriented SSG level with SOC, showing that the fixed-charge scheme enables accurate evaluation of SOC-induced energy differences at low computational cost. The characteristic energy scale among oriented SSA structures is only approximately 0.29 meV per magnetic atom, about 300 times smaller than that of distinct SSA structures, suggesting that calculations with SOC confined to the lowest-energy manifold of oriented SSA structures are sufficient for reliable predictions. These results demonstrate that oriented SSG-based enumeration, combined with the two-step calculations for SSA and oriented SSA structures, provides an efficient and robust route for large-scale magnetic-structure prediction.

candidates.authors: Yuhui Li, Sike Zeng, Yutong Yu, Renzheng Xiong, Yu-Jun Zhao, Xiaobing Chen, Qihang Liu
candidates.abstract: Given the scarcity of experimentally confirmed magnetic structures, the reliable prediction of magnetic ground states is crucial yet remains a long-sought challenge due to the complex magnetic potential energy landscape. Here, we propose a symmetry-guided framework that systematically generates realistic magnetic configurations without requiring any experimental input or prior assumptions such as propagation vectors. The framework incorporates the recently developed oriented spin space group formalism, which captures symmetry-breaking pathways induced by both magnetic ordering and spin-orbit coupling. By performing nonrelativistic and relativistic first-principles calculations, we further establish the energy ladder of the generated magnetic configurations. Exemplified by three prominent unconventional magnets MnTe, Mn 3 Sn , and CoNb 3 S 6 , we demonstrate that only a few dozen first-principles calculations are sufficient to identify the ground-state magnetic structure. To demonstrate the universality and robustness of our approach, we conduct large-scale benchmark tests on the MAGNDATA database. Our framework successfully reproduces experimentally reported magnetic structures for 73% of the surveyed materials. Furthermore, in a high-throughput first-principles benchmark involving 305 compounds, 82% of experimentally reported magnetic geometries are accurately captured within an energy tolerance of 5 meV per magnetic atom from the computed ground state. Beyond reproducing known magnetic configurations, our framework further predicts a variety of low-energy metastable phases, including altermagnets, spin-orbit magnets, and noncollinear antiferromagnets with spin splitting or geometric Hall effect. Our approach is implemented as the open online program SPINGEN, establishing a general and efficient route toward large-scale prediction of magnetic structures and unconventional magnetic phases.

We present FlakeForge, an open-source pipeline from raw optical images of a marker-patterned chip to a lithography-ready, multilayer design file. It scores flakes for device usability, aligns and scales each image from its markers, fits the user's device design to each selected flake's contour and connects every contact to a bond pad by a trace routed around all earlier devices, so no two overlap. Adapting it to a new material, marker design or device dimensions requires only configuration, with no training data; a new device type requires only its geometry definition.

candidates.abstract: Integrating energy storage directly into microelectronic platforms remains a major challenge. Although solid-state micro-supercapacitors (MSCs) have been previously demonstrated, most still rely on liquid or solvent-containing gel electrolytes, which require additional encapsulation and complicate device integration. Here, we demonstrate wafer-scale fabrication of all-2D, fully solid-state MSCs by combining conductive Ti3C2Tz MXene electrodes with a natural vermiculite (VMT) clay solid electrolyte. Both materials are solution-processable and can be independently patterned using microelectronics compatible fabrication techniques, allowing for their integration across 4-inch Si/SiO2 wafers. The resulting devices showcase an active stack of only 28 nm thick, with an areal capacitance of 205 uF/cm2 and volumetric energy density of ~15.5 mWh/cm3. Notably, this work introduces a patterned 2D clay as a solid electrolyte in an on-chip electrochemical energy-storage device, extending the role of layered materials beyond electrodes to ion-conducting components. To investigate device behavior and degradation, we employ non-destructive imaging ellipsometry to map individual layer thicknesses and extract the spatial distribution of MXene conductivity across the chip. This approach reveals localized changes in electrode properties following prolonged electrochemical cycling, providing insight into degradation processes that are difficult to capture using conventional spatially averaged measurements. Together, these results establish a route towards fully solid-state, all-2D energy-storage devices and highlight the potential of solution-processable layered materials for integration into microelectronic systems.

candidates.abstract: The origin of superconductivity near 30~K in Ba$_{0.6}$K$_{0.4}$BiO$_3$ has remained a long-standing puzzle. Tunneling experiments give an electron--boson coupling $λ\approx 0.7$--1.2, whereas density-functional calculations give $λ\approx 0.3$, concentrated in the breathing mode near 50--70~meV. We propose that the missing coupling of about 0.7 comes from dynamical charge fluctuations at Q=(pi,pi,pi)/a, the ordering vector of the charge-disproportionated parent compound, and introduce an overdamped boson model to describe them. Using a tight-binding fit to the conduction band found from density-functional calculations at $x=0.4$, we show that such a boson scatters electrons strongly only on hot lines of the Fermi surface, small loops around the $\langle 111\rangle$ directions where k and k+Q are both at the Fermi level. We derive closed-form self-energies, quasiparticle residues and band reconstructions, including shadow bands and hot-line pseudogaps for long-range correlations, and show that a sum rule fixes the Fermi-surface-averaged coupling independently of the boson frequency and correlation length. Combining the LDA phonon with an overdamped mode of frequency $ω_m\approx 25$~meV and coupling $λ\approx 0.7$, anisotropic Eliashberg calculations reproduce $T_c\approx 25$--30~K for correlation lengths of two to three lattice spacings and predict a gap enhanced by a factor of 3--4 on the hot loops. For longer correlation lengths an $s$-wave state competes closely with a sign-changing $T_{2g}$ state confined to the hot loops. In the random-phase approximation for an extended Hubbard model, the boson emerges naturally near a charge instability at $R$, but purely electronic fluctuations are too weak and too long-ranged; coupling to the breathing-mode lattice distortion is one possible way to strengthen them.

candidates.abstract: We develop a systematic asymptotic analysis of the exact finite-population solution of Granovetter's threshold model, in which a single initial instigator triggers a cascade among agents with independently distributed adoption thresholds. By expressing the propagation probability as an order-statistic boundary-crossing event, we formulate its macroscopic large-deviation rate as a constrained relative-entropy minimization problem. For Beta-distributed thresholds, we obtain explicit solutions for all shape parameters $α$ and $β$, identifying four possible optimal empirical threshold profiles: fully free, fully pinned, pinned--free, and free--pinned. These profiles determine both the exponential probability of macroscopic cascades and the threshold configurations responsible for their occurrence. Importance-sampling estimates confirm the analytical rate functions, while sequential Monte Carlo simulations independently reproduce the predicted optimal profiles. We also revisit the critical scaling near $α_c=1$ and confirm the principal finite-size scaling laws: the mean active fraction decays as $N^{-1/2}$ for uniform thresholds and as $N^{-1}$ for $α=1$ and $0<β<1$. In the latter regime, we further derive an explicit scaling function for the logarithmic critical window from the microscopic branching-process limit. Our results provide a general framework for determining the probabilities and characteristic configurations of rare collective events in threshold-driven cascade processes

candidates.abstract: We theoretically investigate twisted bilayer graphene (tTBG) heterostructures subjected to circularly polarized light. Inversion symmetry is broken through the combined application of an out-of-plane electric field and the incorporation of insulating substrates, enabling precise control of the valley degrees of freedom and associated topological phases. We identify a regime in which the valley degeneracy is lifted: one valley retains a gapless, linear Dirac-like dispersion, whereas the other develops a finite band gap and becomes electronically inactive. The interplay between Floquet driving and inversion-symmetry breaking induces topological phase transitions characterized by Chern numbers C = -2, C = -1, and C = 0, together with the emergence of perfectly valley-polarized domain-wall channels. Furthermore, magnetic asymmetry arising from proximity to adjacent two-dimensional ferromagnetic contacts enables spin-valley filtering. These findings establish the potential of graphene-based heterostructures as highly tunable systems for controlling spin and valley degrees of freedom.

candidates.abstract: Quantum oscillations are an essential probe of the Fermi surface in conductors, and cyclotron masses extracted using the Lifshitz-Kosevich (LK) formula are used to evaluate correlation strength and the assignment of topological states. These masses depend on choices in signal processing, including the field window, method of background subtraction, and spectral window applied before the Fourier transform. These choices are often guided by visual inspection, yet they can alter spectral features and bias the extracted masses. We show that (1) representing a finite field interval by a single effective field can underestimate the cyclotron mass; (2) polynomial background subtraction can attenuate and shift low-frequency peaks; and (3) spectral tapering can reduce mass bias from leakage between neighboring peaks, at the cost of frequency resolution. We demonstrate these effects using numerical calculations and Shubnikov-de Haas experiments on the rare-earth tritellurides RTe3 (R = Pr, Nd, Gd, Tb) with a dense low-frequency spectrum in the charge ordered state. The examples reveal masses shifting by tens of percent with the field window, apparent peak shifts produced only by the background fit, and a reported departure from LK behavior that resolves into two neighboring frequencies.

This study explores the relationship between stoichiometry, structural phase, and electronic transport in niobium sulfoselenide (NbSxSe2-x) thin films. In this study, low-dimensional TMD films were grown with molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) to investigate the effects of varying chalcogen (sulfur and selenium) content in NbSxSe2-x alloys. We focus on tuning electrical resistivity along with the transition from metallic-to-semiconducting behavior through compositional control. These MBE grown films were characterized using in-vacuo x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) to analyze the chemical composition. Electrical resistivity of the films and their temperature coefficient of resistance (TCR) were extracted to determine their metallic and semiconducting behavior. Our results show that increasing sulfur content induces a transition from metallic to semiconducting behavior in NbSe2, accompanied by a rise in resistivity. This work highlights the potential for compositional tuning of TMDs for applications in tunable nanoelectronics.

candidates.abstract: In our recent work (Phys. Rev. B \textbf{113}, 224503 (2026)), we showed numerically that rapidly sweeping the bias current of a current-biased Josephson junction threshold detector (CBJJ-JTD) drives it out of equilibrium. This substantially reduces the effect of thermal noise on microwave detection and may enable threshold detection near the energy of a single microwave photon. The scheme requires very low damping ($β\leq 10^{-4}$) and a very fast bias-current sweep ($v/β\geq 1$), both of which are difficult to achieve with available junctions and low-pass-filtered cryogenic measurement lines. Here we propose a more experimentally accessible nonequilibrium threshold detector based on a high-frequency flux-driven direct-current superconducting quantum interference device (DC-SQUID) and investigate it by numerically solving the resistively and capacitively shunted junction (RCSJ) equations. The applied flux drives a circulating supercurrent and sustains nonequilibrium phase dynamics throughout the bias-current sweep, removing the need for a fast sweep or for transient oscillations set by the initial phase. Using typical experimental device parameters, we calculate switching-current distributions (SCDs) with and without a microwave input for both driven and undriven SQUIDs. We quantify detection performance using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and their area under the curve (AUC). The simulations show that high-frequency flux drive reduces the impact of thermal noise and enables statistical discrimination of weak microwave pulses at the single-photon energy scale. We also numerically estimate detector characteristics such as phase selectivity and dynamic range.

candidates.abstract: Altermagnets have spin-split bands without net magnetization. The splitting can come from a spin-dependent nearest-neighbor (NN) hopping anisotropy $t_A$ or from a spin-dependent next-nearest-neighbor (NNN) hopping $t'$. Both change sign under a $90^\circ$ rotation and are present together when the lattice has no mirror planes, yet they have so far been studied only separately. Here we study the two-dimensional square-lattice Hubbard model with both $t_A$ and $t'$, using constrained-path quantum Monte Carlo at $U=4t$ and scanning the electron filling $n$, $t_A$ and $t'$. We find four types of magnetic correlations: Néel, stripe, diagonal, and spiral spin-density-wave. The phase diagram depends on both hoppings together. Diagonal correlations require finite $t_A$ and are suppressed by $t'$. Stripe correlations appear only once $t'$ is large enough to overcome the diagonal tendency set by $t_A$. Néel correlations survive at large $t_A$ and large $t'$, where the NNN model alone gives stripe or spiral correlations. The noninteracting susceptibility matches the dominant wavevector at small $t'$, but not the Néel correlations at $t'\geq0.3$, which come from the interaction. Finite-size scaling with three lattice sizes is consistent with long-range order only near half filling; at the stripe, spiral and diagonal points we tested, the structure factor per site extrapolates to zero. The joint behavior persists up to $U=6t$.

candidates.abstract: The transport properties of type-II superconductors in the mixed state below the superconducting transition temperature, $T_c$, remain difficult to interpret because superconducting and dissipative processes coexist in the presence of a magnetic field. To investigate this regime in NbN thin films, we measured the field-dependent sheet resistance ($R^M_{xx}$) and Hall resistance ($R^M_{xy}$) below $T_c$ in Van der Pauw geometry for 4-nm-thick NbN films on sapphire and silicon substrates at driving currents of 1 mA and 2 mA. By combining the longitudinal response with the antisymmetrized Hall signal, we use a phenomenological current-partition model to estimate the dissipative and superconducting current contributions. From this analysis, we estimate the field-dependent superconducting current together with the Hall-derived effective dissipative carrier density and mobility. We also observe an even-in-field transverse signal whose magnitude depends strongly on the driving current. We discuss this signal as a possible mixed-state response involving the magnetic and supercurrent texture of Abrikosov vortices, vortex dynamics, and Cooper-pair current redistribution. The present measurements do not uniquely distinguish vortex, condensate, or combined contributions. The model provides a practical way to compare the longitudinal and transverse mixed-state responses without implying a direct spatial separation of the two current channels.

candidates.abstract: Generalizing de Gennes' ant-in-the-labyrinth concept, we consider a chiral random walker on a percolation cluster at criticality. The fully chiral ant clings to obstacle boundaries and traces the fractal hulls of the cluster, spreading with the exact walk dimension $7/4$ until its orbit closes. Because the cluster contains holes on all scales, the ensemble spreads superdiffusively, $\langle r^2\rangle\sim t^{89/84}$, carried by a diminishing fraction of walkers whose orbits are still open. Both exponents follow from percolation geometry alone, and agree well with large-scale numerical simulations. When the walker turns chirally only with probability $χ<1$, superdiffusion gives way to the subdiffusion of the ant at a crossover time set by both exponents, with a diffusion coefficient enhanced by $(1-χ)^{-2/d_w}$. The relation between crossover time and diffusion coefficient does not depend on how chirality is realized, offering a direct test for chiral tracers in disordered media.

candidates.abstract: We demonstrate that local pressure provides an effective means of engineering reconfigurable quantum confinement in MoTe2 homobilayers. By applying a smooth, spatially varying pressure profile, we show that the confinement geometry can be continuously tuned from a conventional quantum dot to a quantum ring, with the emergence of annular confinement being a distinctive feature of AB-stacked bilayers. This crossover originates from the pressure-induced spatial modulation in the electronic parameters, which produces an off-center minimum in the effective confinement potential, thereby redistributing the ground-state probability density away from the center and giving rise to an annular confinement geometry. In the quantum-ring regime, a perpendicular magnetic field gives rise to a flux-periodic energy spectrum and persistent currents, providing characteristic signatures of the Aharonov-Bohm effect. By coupling the pressure-induced quantum ring to source and drain leads, we further demonstrate pronounced Aharonov-Bohm conductance oscillations, accompanied by real-space current patterns exhibiting constructive and destructive interference at integer and half-integer magnetic flux quanta, respectively. These findings establish locally pressurized MoTe2 bilayers as a lithography-free platform for reconfigurable quantum confinement and realizing pressure-tunable Aharonov-Bohm interferometry in two dimensional materials.

candidates.abstract: This paper formulates an extended framework for a hybrid physically informed data-driven model of low-pressure carburizing (LPC), in which diffusive carbon transport in austenite is described by a physical equation, whereas the effective carbon flux across the gas-metal interface is treated as an unknown boundary forcing to be identified from experimental and process data. The basis for this formulation is that, in LPC, the most uncertain part of the model is not bulk diffusion but the transient surface kinetics of carbon uptake by the metal. In contrast to direct empirical relationships of the 'process regime-result' type, the proposed scheme uses machine learning as a closure operator for the boundary condition in the diffusion problem. This operator is calibrated using carbon concentration profiles, integral mass gain, surface concentration, effective case depth, and additional process measurements. Theoretically, the model is positioned as an operator-learning problem in a system constrained by a partial differential equation, physical flux constraints, inverse-problem regularization, and uncertainty quantification. The relationships between the proposed approach and physics-informed neural networks, operator learning, dynamic-system identification, boundary-operator learning, and boundary-control problems are considered. The mathematical formulation, calibration functional, identifiability conditions, preliminary tuning algorithm, and online adaptation scheme are formulated. The proposed approach is considered as a computational basis for developing interpretable digital support for LPC processes.

candidates.abstract: Domain walls in the perpendicular bias of rhombohedral (ABC-stacked) graphene bind valley-resolved interface modes whose signed number is fixed by a bulk-difference invariant. We determine which values of this invariant are reachable when the layer potentials are arbitrary monotone profiles, as produced by screening, and when the interlayer couplings vary from bond to bond. Within the single-particle continuum model, the invariant of an $m$-layer stack equals the difference of occupied angular weights of the zero-momentum levels, which reduces the classification to the ordering of those levels. At equal coupling, nonlinear monotone potentials reproduce exactly the set of invariants of linear potentials, also under the requirement of a common energy gap: screening moves phase boundaries but creates no new invariant values. With bond-dependent coupling, we characterize all occupied configurations. The range of attainable invariants is unchanged, but the gaps inside it are filled, beginning at five layers. Reflection-symmetric stacks realize a large subfamily with a guaranteed common gap, and lower bounds on single-bulk gaps complete the set of invariants with a common global gap for five and six layers. Among the examples is an eight-layer domain wall defined purely by gates, whose number of co-propagating channels per valley switches from 8 to 16 as the gate strength increases. Exact transfer-matrix calculations of the interface spectrum reproduce every predicted signed crossing count. A norm bound gives the minimum spread of interlayer coupling compatible with a prescribed gap.

Can a one-particle approximation with the correct total spin intensity nevertheless misestimate the depth of a depression in the local spin spectrum? For spin-created states with odd final quasiparticle number and nonzero one-particle weight, restoring multiparticle weight shallows the depression on 24 sites and deepens it on both 1,536-site shapes and the 3,456- and 6,144-site tori, as judged by the median paired correction at each of two energy resolutions. RPA and FLEX calculations based on this model consistently indicate a dominant $d_{x^2-y^2}$-wave pairing instability. These results establish La$_4$Ni$_3$O$_8$ as a system whose electronic structure closely resembles that of hole-doped cuprates, suggesting that the electronic pockets near the $Γ$- and $A$-points, which are characteristic of infinite-layer nickelates, may not be essential for superconductivity. The calculated superconducting transition temperature ($T_C$) is approximately 10\,K, in good agreement with experimental observations.

candidates.abstract: AmorphGen is an open-source Python package for generating and analyzing amorphous structures from a composition or a crystal. Chemically informed rules estimate initial densities and assign separation and coordination constraints. Three routes are available: random placement followed by relaxation, melt-quench from a crystal, and a hybrid route that anneals and quenches random structures. ASE provides access to classical and machine-learning potentials, with GPU batching for selected backends. Analysis tools compute coordination numbers, bond angles, rings, and X-ray or neutron structure factors for comparison with measurements. An optional interface to the FEFF code computes extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectra. For amorphous Ga2O3, TiO2 and InGaZnO4, the cation coordination numbers are close to reference models and measurements, and the X-ray structure factors reproduce the main measured peaks. The EXAFS spectra for Ga2O3 and InGaZnO4 also capture the dominant first-shell features observed experimentally. The hybrid route reduces bonding defects in SiO2 and As and builds the first sharp diffraction peak of SiO2. By simplifying ensemble generation and standardizing structural assessment, AmorphGen makes it practical to compare amorphous models across compositions, potentials, and preparation routes, and to screen new amorphous compositions.

Zinc oxide (ZnO) is the archetypal absorber for this task: UV-selective, earth-abundant, non-toxic, and processable at low temperature from solution. Operating it without bias, however, requires a built-in asymmetry that pristine ZnO rarely provides. Because the literature is organized by material or mechanism, the design logic remains obscured. Here we organize the field by engineering strategy, identifying five families of levers (junction and built-in-field engineering, doping and defect control, polarization coupling, interface/surface and photoelectrochemical engineering, and architecture and light management) and mapping each onto the metrics it serves and the trade-offs it imposes. A unifying lens is the zero-bias doping paradox: raising carrier density narrows the depletion region that zero-bias collection needs, so the self-powered optimum differs from the biased one. We flag the detectivity, speed, and active-area pitfalls that make zero-bias performance easy to overstate, and condense the synthesis into a decision tree linking target metric to strategy and growth route. The remaining bottlenecks (persistent photoconductivity, p-type ZnO, and reporting consistency) are problems of defect control and rigorous measurement, not of new materials.

Here, we introduce a minimal three-band continuum model with separately tunable quantum metric and Berry flux. Employing the Hartree-Fock approach, we find that a conventional s-wave Wigner crystal can develop a hollow charge distribution with depleted density at lattice sites, without a change in symmetry or topology. We show that this density reconstruction occurs even at vanishing Berry curvature and arises from strong quantum metric and the nontrivial angular structure of the form factor. In our model, the continuous crossover between hollow and conventional WCs is accompanied by anomalous direct exchange interactions, nearly vanishing at intermediate quantum metric but enhanced by over an order of magnitude in the strong-metric regime. These results reveal how quantum metric can reshape both the charge distribution and exchange interactions of electron crystals beyond simple wave-function delocalization.

candidates.abstract: Li-rich battery cathodes (LixMyOz, where x > y) have sparked significant attention for their high energy densities, but their practical application is currently limited by structural instabilities associated with high-valent redox. Recent work has demonstrated reversible high-potential (de)lithiation with low voltage hysteresis in Li4FeSbO6 (LFSO), but the stabilization mechanism for this unique charging behavior is not fully understood, limiting our ability to apply insights from LFSO to more earth-abundant cathodes. In this paper, we present a covalent Sb-O bonding network in LFSO which is facilitated by the p-block orbital character of Sb. Using ab initio computational modeling, we identify this bonding state and indicate its contributions to crystal stability; we also identify a signature for this bonding network using theoretical and experimental element-specific X-ray spectroscopy. Substituting Sb with other p-block elements preserves this stabilizing bond, pointing to a family of new cathode chemistries beyond LFSO. This work establishes a design principle for development of sustainable energy-dense batteries: p-block elements like Sb possess specific orbital-mediated oxygen bonding which contributes to stability of high-valent layered oxide cathodes.

candidates.abstract: The structural, optoelectronic, mechanical, thermodynamic, and thermoelectric properties of kesterite Cu2ZnSnS4 were investigated using density functional theory. The mBJ and HSE06 approaches yield band gaps of 0.88 and 1.55 eV, respectively. Optical calculations reveal high absorption, with the onset in the 0.8-1.0 eV range. Hydrostatic compression from 0 to 30 kbar decreases the lattice parameters and increases the band gap. The elastic constants satisfy the Born stability criterion, and B/G $>$ 1.75 indicates plastic behavior. Phonon calculations confirm dynamic stability. In the temperature range from 0 to 1000 K, the Helmholtz free energy decreases, the vibrational entropy increases, and the heat capacity approaches a plateau above 500 K. The thermoelectric properties were investigated in the temperature range from 100 to 1000 K. The Seebeck coefficient remains positive, peaking at approximately 310 $μ$V/K at 250 K and decreasing to 239 $μ$V/K at 1000 K. These results encourage the investigation of Cu2ZnSnS4 as a good candidate for thermoelectric power conversion.

candidates.abstract: Predicting a material's behavior from its atomic structure is a longstanding goal of the physical sciences. The electronic and phonon densities of states (eDOS and phDOS) govern key electronic, optical, vibrational, and thermodynamic properties, yet their calculation using density functional theory (DFT) is costly: about 60% of Materials Project entries lack eDOS and over 80% lack phDOS. Existing crystal-to-spectrum models rely on pooled structural representations and pointwise regression, which blur spectral features and violate total-state conservation. Here we introduce DeepDOSReasoner, a physics-grounded framework that decodes spectra through atom-to-energy source attention and refines the normalized DOS through learned continuity-equation transport, enforcing nonnegativity and total-state conservation by construction. DeepDOSReasoner achieves the highest prediction accuracy across all evaluated metrics for both eDOS and phDOS, recovers element-resolved contributions without supervision, and most reliably identifies rare valence-band (VB) gaps. In a prospective screen of 8,106 uncharted materials validated by new DFT calculations, its predictions remain the most accurate among the methods evaluated, with 25 of its top 50 candidates confirmed as VB-gap materials. Three case studies spanning substituted compounds, photovoltaic chalcogenides, and a high-entropy alloy demonstrate transfer across materials classes. Ablations confirm that both stages are necessary, while the model retains comparable accuracy when trained on only 25% of the data. Predicting spectra in milliseconds enables exhaustive screening; we release predictions filling the missing eDOS for 91,405 and phDOS for 127,768 Materials Project entries. DeepDOSReasoner provides a blueprint for integrating machine learning with physical reasoning toward high-throughput spectral screening and autonomous materials discovery.

candidates.abstract: Multi-agent frameworks are attracting increasing attention as a means of autonomously driving complex, long-running workflows in first-principles materials modeling. However, such frameworks commonly organize AI agents by computational task or scientific role. When scaled across many materials, this organization can require repeated transfers of material-specific context and complicate persistent execution and resource coordination. Here, we introduce AgenticMM, a material-centered multi-agent architecture in which each material has a persistent agent that owns its complete workflow and retains its scientific context, while a persistent coordinator allocates shared resources, mediates communication, and tracks campaign progress. AgenticMM is designed to incorporate reusable, prompt-based skills as modular definitions of these workflows. Using DefectSkills prompts, we demonstrate the feasibility of AgenticMM through a multistage point-defect campaign in which material-specific agents concurrently perform host electronic-structure, phase-stability, and intrinsic-defect calculations for five chemically diverse semiconductors.

candidates.abstract: This study demonstrates pyroelectric energy harvesting from a steady heat source using active piezoelectric thermal switching in a PZT/Si bimorph cantilever. The same PZT layer serves as both the mechanical actuator and the pyroelectric energy-conversion element. Dual output electrodes enable separation of the pyroelectric and piezoelectric signals. Pyroelectric energy harvesting is experimentally demonstrated at frequencies up to 110 Hz and temperature differences as small as 5 K. Comparison with the response predicted from the independently measured pyroelectric coefficient, together with transient thermal simulations, identifies dynamic interfacial heat transfer as a key limitation to high-frequency operation. This work demonstrates a compact MEMS approach for higher-frequency pyroelectric energy harvesting from low-grade steady heat sources.

candidates.abstract: We investigate the normal-state electrical properties of ultrathin amorphous Mo$_{1-x}$Si$_x$ films deposited by DC magnetron co-sputtering over a broad range of compositions and thicknesses. Films with Si contents of $x = 0.14$ to $0.5$ were deposited on Si/SiO$_2$ and Si/Si$_3$N$_4$ substrates (monocrystalline Si with SiO$_2$ and S$_3$N$_4$ buffer layers respectfully); X-ray diffraction confirms an amorphous structure across the full composition range, while X-ray reflectometry is used to verify film thicknesses. The room-temperature sheet resistance ranges from 110 to 1990 $Ω/\square$, corresponding to resistivities of 125-478 $μΩ\cdot$cm. The sheet resistance generally increases with increasing Si content and decreasing film thickness, although the coupled variation of composition and thickness limits the quantitative separation of these effects. Additional measurements on thicker reference films show superconducting transition temperatures between 5.2 and 7.7 K, with $T_c$ decreasing monotonically at higher Si contents. A comparison of films on different substrate types shows no systematic difference between Si/SiO$_2$ and Si/Si$_3$N$_4$, while films on Al$_2$O$_3$ exhibit elevated sheet resistance at the lower thicknesses. These results characterize the accessible parameter space of our deposition process and provide a basis for the selection of film stoichiometry for detector fabrication.
